review.tagline: Python library that extracts source-grounded structured data from text using LLMs
review.summary: LangExtract is a Python library that takes a prompt and few-shot examples, runs an LLM over unstructured text, and returns structured extractions mapped to exact character spans in the source. Long documents are handled by chunking, parallel workers and multiple passes. Results save to JSONL and render as an interactive HTML review page. Backends include Gemini, OpenAI and local Ollama models.
review.audience: Python developers extracting structured data from long documents
strengths: Each extraction is grounded to a character span; ungrounded results get char_interval = None
Chunking, parallel workers and multiple passes for long documents (max_workers, extraction_passes)
Gemini, OpenAI and Ollama supported, plus a plugin system for custom providers
Generates a self-contained interactive HTML view of extractions in context
weaknesses: Output schema is driven by few-shot examples; poor examples cause alignment warnings and weaker results
Ollama provider does not support output_schema
Controlled generation is documented mainly for Gemini; cloud models need an API key
Library only, with no server or UI beyond the HTML visualization
needs: Needs Gemini, OpenAI or Vertex AI API key for cloud models, Ollama for local models
Models: Gemini, OpenAI, Ollama, Vertex AI, OpenAI-compatible endpoints
